plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (MgF2/Al2O3 defect cavity stack) based on prior iteration results. Candidate 0 achieved target_score 0.199 with a simple periodic geometry (45/38 nm mirrors, 90 nm defect), while optimized candidates reached 0.31-0.32 but with erratic thickness distributions. Feedback directives specify constraining initialization to neighborhoods around Candidate 0's verified geometry: mirror layers 35-55 nm, defect cavity 80-100 nm. Three routes proposed: (1) Tight-constraint refinement of original 17-layer MgF2/Al2O3 stack, (2) Expanded 25-layer version for stronger visible/IR rejection, (3) Alternative HfO2/SiO2 material pair at 21 layers for higher index contrast. All routes preserve the defect-cavity-in-periodic-stack principle from evidence on 1-D photonic crystal UV filters.

routes.title: Tight-constraint MgF2/Al2O3 defect cavity refinement with bounded thickness initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness initialization to neighborhoods around Candidate 0's verified geometry (mirror layers 35-55 nm, defect cavity 80-100 nm) will enable the optimizer to refine phase-matching within a proven topology rather than rediscovering basic periodicity, leading to improved target scores while maintaining physical validity.
routes.design_principle: 1-D photonic crystal with periodic Bragg mirrors sandwiching a central defect cavity layer, using Transfer Matrix Method optimization with experimental optical constants. Mirror layers oscillate between low-index MgF2 and high-index Al2O3 at quarter-wave optical thickness for the UV passband center.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (MgF2/Al2O3) x4 | MgF2 | defect_Al2O3 | MgF2 | (Al2O3/MgF2) x4 | fused_silica. Total 17 finite layers: 8 mirror pairs plus 1 central defect layer.
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for planar multilayer interference
Defect mode in 1-D photonic crystal creates narrow transmission peak within stopband
Quarter-wave stack principle for Bragg mirrors
expected_advantages: Reduced search dimensionality through bounded initialization
Faster convergence to local optimum near proven geometry
Maintains physical validity from prior iteration
known_risks: May converge to local optimum inferior to global solution
Limited exploration of alternative thickness regimes
MgF2/Al2O3 index contrast may be insufficient for wide stopband
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 17-layer defect-cavity thin-film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: MgF2, Al2O3, MgF2, Al2O3, MgF2, Al2O3, MgF2, Al2O3, MgF2, Al2O3 (defect cavity), MgF2, Al2O3, MgF2, Al2O3, MgF2, Al2O3, MgF2. Initialize layer thicknesses with mirror layers (all except layer 10) bounded to 35-55 nm range and defect cavity layer (layer 10) bounded to 80-100 nm range. Optimize all 17 thicknesses using differential evolution to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm band while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Total layer count fixed at 17. No metal layers. Use conventional dielectric optical constants for MgF2 and Al2O3. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Refinement of route_01 based on feedback directives: constrain thickness initialization to neighborhoods around Candidate 0's verified geometry (mirror layers 35-55 nm, defect cavity 80-100 nm) to reduce search dimensionality and force optimizer to refine phase-matching rather than rediscovering basic periodicity.

routes.title: Expanded 25-layer MgF2/Al2O3 defect cavity for enhanced visible/IR rejection
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing mirror pair count from 4 to 6 per side (25 total layers) will widen and deepen the stopband in visible and near-IR ranges while maintaining UV passband transmission, improving the multi-band suppression objective without exceeding the 30-layer manufacturing limit.
routes.design_principle: Same defect-cavity-in-periodic-stack principle as route_01, but with expanded Bragg mirror sections to increase stopband reflectivity. Additional layers provide more degrees of freedom for spectral shaping while preserving the central defect resonance.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (MgF2/Al2O3) x6 | MgF2 | defect_Al2O3 | MgF2 | (Al2O3/MgF2) x6 | fused_silica. Total 25 finite layers: 12 mirror pairs plus 1 central defect layer.
manufacturing_considerations: increased deposition time and complexity with more layers
theory_basis: Bragg mirror stopband width and depth increase with pair count
Defect mode transmission peak remains narrow regardless of mirror count
Transfer Matrix Method scales linearly with layer count
expected_advantages: Stronger visible and IR suppression from additional mirror pairs
Wider stopband coverage across 300-1100 nm range
More optimization degrees of freedom for spectral shaping
known_risks: Increased total thickness may introduce stress or adhesion issues
More layers increase deposition time and cost
May not significantly improve UV passband if limited by material absorption

Initialize layer thicknesses with mirror layers (all except layer 14) bounded to 35-55 nm range and defect cavity layer (layer 14) bounded to 80-100 nm range. Total layer count fixed at 25. No metal layers. Use conventional dielectric optical constants for MgF2 and Al2O3. routes.revision_reason: Diversification from route_01 by increasing layer count from 17 to 25 to test hypothesis that additional mirror pairs improve stopband rejection in visible and IR bands while maintaining UV passband. Same material pair and defect-cavity principle preserved.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 defect cavity stack at 21 layers for higher index contrast
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing MgF2/Al2O3 with HfO2/SiO2 material pair will increase refractive index contrast, enabling wider stopband and deeper rejection in visible/IR bands with fewer total layers, while maintaining UV transparency in the 255-280 nm passband.
routes.design_principle: Same defect-cavity-in-periodic-stack principle, but using HfO2 (high index ~2.0-2.2 in UV) and SiO2 (low index ~1.5) for higher contrast than MgF2/Al2O3. Evidence indicates HfO2/SiO2 stacks are common for UV filters with ion-assisted deposition for stability.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (SiO2/HfO2) x5 | SiO2 | defect_HfO2 | SiO2 | (HfO2/SiO2) x5 | fused_silica. Total 21 finite layers: 10 mirror pairs plus 1 central defect layer.
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 requires ion-assisted deposition for density and stability
SiO2/HfO2 pair well-established for UV applications
theory_basis: Higher index contrast produces wider photonic bandgap
HfO2 transparent in UV with appropriate deposition conditions
SiO2 provides low-index contrast layer with excellent UV transparency
expected_advantages: Wider stopband from higher index contrast
Potentially fewer layers needed for same rejection performance
HfO2/SiO2 well-characterized for UV filter applications
known_risks: HfO2 may exhibit absorption near 255 nm if not properly deposited
Index inhomogeneity reported for evaporated HfO2 without ion assistance
Material pair change may require re-optimization of entire thickness profile
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer defect-cavity thin-film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2 (defect cavity), SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2. Initialize layer thicknesses with mirror layers (all except layer 12) bounded to 35-55 nm range and defect cavity layer (layer 12) bounded to 80-100 nm range. Optimize all 21 thicknesses using differential evolution to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm band while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Total layer count fixed at 21. No metal layers. Use conventional dielectric optical constants for HfO2 and SiO2 appropriate for UV wavelength range. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Material substitution from route_01: replacing MgF2/Al2O3 with HfO2/SiO2 to test hypothesis that higher index contrast improves stopband performance. Layer count adjusted to 21 (intermediate between 17 and 25) to balance contrast benefit against deposition complexity. Same defect-cavity topology and initialization bounds preserved for fair comparison.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:199509322 supports 1-D photonic crystal defect cavity design with periodic (L/2 H L/2) m units and AR coatings, directly motivating the defect-cavity topology in all three routes
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:211025653 documents HfO2/SiO2 as established UV filter material pair with ion-assisted deposition for stability, motivating route_01_refine_03 material substitution
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:16516444 supports ALD for precise thickness control in UV coatings, informing manufacturing considerations for all routes
Prior iteration route_01 results (best_target_score 0.324, Candidate 0 geometry 45/38 nm mirrors with 90 nm defect) directly inform the bounded initialization constraints in all refinement routes
unresolved_decisions: Optimal material pair for 255-280 nm passband remains uncertain: MgF2/Al2O3 proven in iteration but may have limited index contrast; HfO2/SiO2 higher contrast but requires verification of UV transparency at 255 nm
Optimal layer count between 17 and 30 layers not determined: testing 17, 21, and 25 layers across routes to identify sweet spot between performance and manufacturability
Incidence angle and polarization not specified in original request: all routes assume normal incidence and unpolarized light, may need angular robustness analysis in future iterations
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
